definitions.explanation: Flat stones laid on the ground to form a path or surface. Used for garden paths, walkways, plazas, and streets.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}に{敷石|しきいし}を{並|なら}べる。
examples.english: To lay paving stones in the garden.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}で{敷石|しきいし}が{濡|ぬ}れて{滑|すべ}りやすい。
examples.english: The paving stones are wet from the rain and slippery.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{神社|じんじゃ}の{参道|さんどう}には{苔|こけ}の{生|は}えた{敷石|しきいし}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: Moss-covered paving stones line the approach to the old shrine.

notes: Composed of {敷|し}く (to lay, to spread) + {石|いし} (stone). Common collocations: {敷石|しきいし}を{敷|し}く (to lay paving stones), {敷石|しきいし}の{道|みち} (a stone-paved path). Found in traditional Japanese gardens, shrine approaches ({参道|さんどう}), and historical districts. Related: {石畳|いしだたみ} (stone pavement — a broader term for stone-paved surfaces), {飛|と}び{石|いし} (stepping stones placed at intervals).
